newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway Brundtland governed some of world's richest.
newsitem.headline: Norway Brundtland governed some of world's richest.

text.p: Norway's veteran Prime Minister Gro Harlem Brundtland, who announced on Wednesday she is stepping down, is a natural-born political slugger who has ruled one of the richest countries in the world for a dozen years.
Brundtland, 57, dominated Norwegian politics through the 1980s and 90s.
She will hand over power to Labour Party leader Thorbjoern Jagland on Friday and said there would be no change in economic policies.
Her challenges have been how to distribute billions of dollars in oil and gas revenue to just 4.3 million people and give Norway a say in Europe although it rejected membership of the European Union.

Prime minister for almost 12 years, Brundtland may now seek to develop her reputation further as an international diplomat. Her name has been mentioned as a possible successor to U.N. Secretary General Boutros Boutros Ghali.
Many commentators said she was devastated by Norwegians' rejection of European Union membership in 1994 despite her campaign to persuade them to join along with neighbours Sweden and Finland.

Brundtland had fought herself out of tight spots before, but the lifelong social democrat lost an uphill battle to persuade Norwegians to accept membership of a bloc they had already rejected once, in 1972.
She has enjoyed international recognition since 1983 as chairwoman of the United Nations World Commission on Environment and Development and is also known as a champion of women's issues.
At the U.N. conference on population in Cairo in September 1994, she angered Moslems and Catholics for saying abortion should be decriminalised and for accusing religious opponents of hypocrisy.
Born in Oslo on April 20, 1939, she graduated from the Harvard School of Public Health in the United States in 1965 and was a doctor in Norway's health service until 1974.
The same year she was appointed environment minister by then prime minister Trygve Bratteli.

Brundtland first took over as prime minister in 1981 from Oddvar Nordli, who retired because of ill-health. But she lost a bid for a full-term in elections eight months later to Conservative Kaare Willoch.
Her fiery temperament in televised debates handicapped that campaign but she later shed her firebrand image to emerge in the 1985 election as an adept politician.
She narrowly lost again to Willoch, but established herself as Labour's uncontested leader.

In 1986 Willoch resigned over a controversial tax bill, and Brundtland led a minority Labour government to power that May. She took over at a time of plunging prices for Norway's main export, North Sea oil, but took a firm grip on a series of political and economic crises.
Brundtland has been prime minister since 1990 when she took over after the collapse of the centre-right government of Conservative premier Jan Syse.
In 1992, she gave up her duties as party chief after her son Joergen, one of four children, committed suicide.
In 1993 general elections, Brundtland retained power as leader of a Labour minority government.
